text:
sara: Heads-up — nightly TP perf job shows a sharp latency spike on the all-reduce path after KV-cache churn. Looks like comm stalls when many small fragments hit the wire (48KB-ish). attaching quick perf dump below.

tj: Can you paste the traces? is this ring vs tree selection doing something weird? :thinking_face: 

sara: paste from perf-top (reduced):
```
cpu 0x1a: nccl:allReduce  28.3%
cpu 0x1b: kernel_selector 12.1%
cuda memcpy  9.6%
comm_wait  18.4% (burst at 48-64KB msgs)
kv_cache_eviction 6.5%
```

lin: hmm — those comm_wait bursts line up with the message-size histogram we saw last week. if the runtime picks ring for 48KB but tree would be better at higher parallel fanout, we might be thrashing NCCL rendezvous. what's the `msgsize_threshold` in kernel_selector atm?

sara: currently 256KB for switching to tree in kernel_selector heuristics. we expected coalescing upstream to keep msgs > 256KB, but KV cache invalidations cause many small prefix requests, so all-reduce sees lots of ~40-60KB fragments.

omar: that explains the latency cliff. ring has O(n) latency per frag and with tiny fragments we pay handshake + kernel launch overhead repeatedly. tree can reduce latency for these sizes if we reduce per-frag fanout, but tree also hurts steady-state throughput for large chunks.

tj: can we try two quick experiments: (A) reduce tree threshold to 64KB and (B) enable an aggressive coalesce window (20ms) for small messages only, to see impact on 8-GPU nightly job?

lin: +1. also add a probe to measure comm/compute overlap: instrument kernel queueing so we can see how often compute waits for all-reduce completion. right now the flame shows compute queues draining then long comm gaps.

sara: created a canary branch with both changes. patch notes: 
```diff
- kernel_selector::tree_threshold = 256 * 1024;
+ kernel_selector::tree_threshold = 64 * 1024;

+ batching::coalesce_window_small_msgs_ms = 20; // applies to msgsize < 128KB
```

ci-bot: triggered CI nightly canary: run/3301234567-canary-8gpus (will post logs when done) :robot_face: 

omar: also add a kv-cache metric: "small_msg_rate" (msgs/sec < 128KB). If small_msg_rate spikes, roll to fallback policy that prefers coalescing before kernel selection. That makes the policy workload-aware.

tj: important to check regressions on throughput for large-batch evals. we don't want to blow up 512-token generation runs. schedule A/B: canary (A=64KB tree) vs baseline (256KB). Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/s.

lin: quick profiling tip — when collecting NCCL traces, set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and use nccl-tests all_reduce microbench to reproduce fragmentation pattern. also capture CUPTI async timeline for overlap view.

sara: thanks. I'll let the canary run and post initial numbers in this thread. if we see win on latency without throughput loss, we can land kernel_selector change and roll coalesce as a feature flag.

tj: awesome. one more thought — maybe we should add a tiny aggregation worker that batches small all-reduce ops in-process before handing off to NCCL, to avoid many separate launches. low-risk toggleable.

omar: agree, but prefer a config-first approach. try heuristics + coalesce window first. aggregation worker can be next sprint if needed.

ci-bot: canary finished: 3301234567-canary-8gpus — artifacts: link to logs (S3), nccl-traces.tar.gz, perf-summary.json

sara: initial diff vs baseline (8 GPU job):
- p50 generation latency: baseline 42ms -> canary 33ms (-21%)
- p95: baseline 310ms -> canary 180ms (-41%)
- tokens/s (large eval): baseline 182k -> canary 178k (-2.2%)
- small_msg_rate in kv-cache metric dropped 3x under coalesce window

lin: nice! small throughput regression is acceptable for 41% p95 drop. we should run the 1000-run stability harness to ensure no edge regressions.

tj: agree. + schedule a ticket to add aggregation worker prototype but keep it low-priority. also add end-to-end perf test that toggles kv-cache eviction patterns to avoid surprises.

sara: created follow-up issues: infra#4123 (stability sweep), runtime#4210 (aggregation worker spike), runtime#4211 (feature-flag rollout for coalesce), and assigned owners. I'll post more logs after extended runs. :thumbsup:

omar: nice detective work — big win if it holds.

sara: thanks team, will update.
